content.value_statement: Accessibility gaps can block users from core product workflows. This skill guides frontend implementation with semantic markup, keyboard support, contrast checks, and screen reader behavior.
actual_capabilities: Guides semantic HTML choices for landmarks, sections, buttons, and links.
Supports accessible form implementation with labels and related inputs.
Prompts keyboard navigation, visible focus states, and focus management for dynamic UI.
Highlights WCAG contrast expectations, including the 4.5:1 minimum noted in the skill.
Covers alternative text, icon labeling, and ARIA attributes for complex components.
Encourages logical heading hierarchy and appropriately sized touch targets.
limitations: It provides implementation guidance, not a full automated accessibility audit.
It does not replace manual testing with screen readers and keyboard-only navigation.
Project-specific component libraries may require additional accessibility rules.
The detailed standard is linked outside the packaged skill and may not be available.

use_cases.title: Review React Components
use_cases.description: Check new React components for labels, roles, focus states, and semantic element choices before merge.

use_cases.title: Improve Product Forms
use_cases.description: Design form fields, validation messages, and error states that work with keyboard and screen reader users.

use_cases.title: Prepare Accessibility Acceptance Criteria
use_cases.description: Translate WCAG-oriented expectations into clear implementation checks for a feature ticket.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner accessibility review for a single UI component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this frontend component for accessibility. Focus on semantic HTML, labels, keyboard use, focus visibility, and screen reader names.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me improve this form for accessibility. Check labels, validation messages, required fields, focus behavior, and helpful error announcements.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Dialog
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a complex interactive pattern.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the accessibility behavior for this modal dialog. Include focus entry, focus trap, close behavior, keyboard support, roles, names, and announcements.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Feature Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across multiple screens or states.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this frontend flow for accessibility risks. Prioritize issues by user impact and include fixes for navigation, headings, contrast, ARIA, and dynamic updates.

output_examples.input: Review a React button and menu pattern for accessibility.
output_examples.output: The review identifies missing keyboard behavior, unclear accessible names, and focus return requirements. It recommends semantic buttons and predictable menu state announcements.

output_examples.input: Improve a signup form with inline validation.
output_examples.output: The response proposes label associations, error text placement, required field messaging, and focus handling after failed submission.

output_examples.input: Check color and heading choices for a dashboard page.
output_examples.output: The response flags contrast risks, heading order problems, and missing landmarks. It suggests stronger text colors and a clearer page structure.

best_practices: Start with semantic HTML before adding ARIA attributes.
Test every interactive control with keyboard-only navigation.
Validate focus order, visible focus indicators, and screen reader names during review.
anti_patterns: Using div elements as buttons without keyboard behavior.
Adding ARIA roles to hide weak semantic structure.
Relying only on automated tools without manual interaction testing.

faq.question: Does this skill run an accessibility scanner?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and review prompts for accessible frontend work.

faq.question: Can it help with React components?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is written for React component work in .tsx and .jsx files.

faq.question: Does it cover keyboard accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers keyboard navigation, focus states, focus management, and interactive controls.

faq.question: Does it explain ARIA usage?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports ARIA decisions for complex UI patterns when semantic HTML is not enough.

faq.question: Does it replace screen reader testing?
faq.answer: No. It should be paired with real keyboard and screen reader testing.

faq.question: Why is there a security warning?
faq.answer: The skill links to a file outside its package. The referenced guidance should be bundled inside the skill.
